messages.author: f53f4ca2c430170d
messages.subject: CmdStan output code... not making sense to me.
parts:
I'm working through CmdStan command.hpp and wondering why the output_stream is used both directly (as a stream, e.g, lines 338-348) as well as through the sample_writer. Is this just pre-writer callbacks cruft?

I'm talking about this code:
if (output_stream) {
std::vector<std::string> names;
names.push_back("lp__");
model.constrained_param_names(names, true, true);

(*output_stream) << names.at(0);
for (size_t i = 1; i < names.size(); ++i) {
(*output_stream) << "," << names.at(i);
}
(*output_stream) << std::endl;
}

I'm modifying a bunch of this kind of stuff on a fork but I can go back and do a pull request with the straight cleanup pieces if that's what's going on .

Krzysztof

messages.subject: Re: CmdStan output code... not making sense to me.
parts:
After some gratuitous hacking on command.hpp there's a version of CmdStan that will write to a postgres database, with the 'model file =' argument hijacked for the database URI string. If you happen to use this you can get around specifying the URI by setting enough environmental variables to make a bare command line 'psql' call open a connection.

https://github.com/sakrejda/cmdstan

I'm going to wait to make this pretty until there's some agreement on output format.

Krzysztof

messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] CmdStan output code... not making sense to me.
parts:
mcmc_writer collects the writer objects to simplify MCMC I/O.
In particular, it grabs the current state of the Markov chain, as
well as the state of the sampler, and writes to the various output
streams (info, error, diagnostic, samples, etc) as necessary. This
way the MCMC code largely doesn’t need to know about the
writers.
